notes: Simulator twin of evaluation/campaigns/expA_dosing.json (experiment A sim-to-real). Same rate (0.5/s), value 1-5, per-device bound 345 (demand ~1.3x), duration 300 s, deadline 60 s, validity 90 s; authority costs as in the campaign (hold 1, stop 1, fence 5); no owner validation rejects (terminal_reject_prob 0: evicon-device never rejects without a bound). Release 066 alignment with the testbed, from the 065 testbed run (inputs only, never outcomes): (1) transport: a command reply that arrives after the authority's dispatch timeout is lost (late_replies=drop), because evicon-authority talks HTTP to evicon-device with a 2 s client timeout (dispatch_timeout_ms 2000) and closes the connection; the 065 twin delivered late replies (a broker reply channel) and so resolved ambiguity the testbed never could (K0: 0.68 vs 0.28). (2) fences: a barrier whose owner receipt has a crash orphan (UNCERTAIN) is aborted and resolves nothing (fence_uncertain=abort), as evicon-authority does; the 065 twin resolved every other identity. (3) fault rates from the realized fault logs of the 240 device-episodes of the 065 campaign: offline 20.5 % of the time with mean 23.7 s (online mean 92 s; the 065 twin: 20 %, 25 s), request drop 1.4 %, reply drop 1.8 %, 6 s delay 1.0 % of the time, and 0.73 crashes between effect and receipt per device-episode = 0.5 % of commands (the 065 twin used 1.3 %). Contracts: sim-k0 ~ K0, sim-k0+F ~ K0F, sim-k2 ~ K2, sim-k2+F ~ K3F (and sim-k1-h45s(+F) ~ K1(F)). One device per episode (the campaign has 4): compare rates, not counts (evaluation/sim_to_real.py). SIMULATION ONLY.
